L13·N10487unmasked layer
Weakly selective boundary-marking neuron: it peaks on tokens that open a new clause/parenthetical reference in expository prose — "see" before a scripture citation, "price" in a label, sentence-initial "We"/"advisable", paragraph newlines — and is strongly suppressed on sub-word fragments of proper nouns (Pent|land, Sway|amb|hu).

L13·N10513unmasked layer

L13·N10971unmasked layer
This neuron is mostly defined by its strong *negative* response to digits embedded in phone numbers / long numeric strings (and adjacent tokens like "rate"), while its weak positive peaks are on filler tokens such as the space separating volume/issue numbers in bibliographic citations, ellipses, and small function words — i.e., it is essentially a digit-sequence suppressor rather than a semantic detector.
